title: AI UX Pattern Contract
description: Machine-readable contract for an AI interface UX pattern. Three consumers: (1) the docs generator, which renders human documentation from this contract plus doc.mdx prose; (2) the MCP server, whose search_patterns and scaffold_pattern tools serve this content to agents at generation time; (3) CI, which validates every /patterns/<id>/pattern.contract.json against this schema. Normative behavior lives in `constraints` as atomic RFC-2119 rules with stable ids; long-form prose lives in doc.mdx, not here.

$schema.description: Optional relative path or URI of this schema, for editor IntelliSense.

id.description: Kebab-case pattern identifier. MUST equal the pattern's directory name under /patterns/ (cross-file check enforced in CI, not here).

version.description: Semver of this contract. Major bumps when a MUST-level constraint is added, removed, or changes meaning.

summary.description: One or two sentences. This is the search card: search_patterns returns it verbatim, so it must stand alone.

status.description: Lifecycle status. `stable` contracts must ship both react and vanilla implementations (enforced below).

supersededBy.description: Id of the pattern that replaces this one. Only valid when status is `deprecated`. Referential existence is checked in CI.

category.description: Primary interaction axis: input (intent capture, prompting), output (rendering generated content), control (interrupt, undo, approval), transparency (reasoning, tool use, provenance), feedback (correction, rating, refinement), context (memory, history, state awareness). Use `tags` for secondary facets.

kind.description: Shape of the reference implementation. `component` (the default when omitted): one component with one state machine. `kit`: multiple cooperating exports woven through host content (e.g. inline anchors + a list + a helper); every anatomy part of a kit must name the export that owns it, per framework.

aliases.description: Alternative names practitioners use for this pattern. Searched by search_patterns.

problem.description: The UX problem this pattern solves, stated as a problem — not a description of the solution.

useWhen.description: Concrete conditions under which an agent or developer should reach for this pattern.

dontUseWhen.description: Conditions under which this pattern is the wrong choice. Required: knowing when not to use a pattern is half its value.

anatomy.description: The named parts of the pattern. scaffold_pattern uses these ids; constraints reference them informally.

states.description: The pattern's state machine. Exactly one state must declare `initial: true`. Transition targets are referentially checked in CI.

allOf.description: Every contract must carry at least one accessibility constraint. Accessibility is a contract field, not an afterthought.
A contract with no MUST-level rule is documentation, not a contract.

constraints.description: Atomic normative rules. Constraint ids are stable within the pattern and are the targets COMPLIANCE.md files trace to; never reuse an id after removing it. Uniqueness of ids is checked in CI.

accessibility.description: Structured accessibility metadata: which WCAG criteria apply and how the pattern behaves for keyboard and screen reader users. Normative a11y rules live in `constraints` with category `accessibility`; this object holds the supporting structure docs and agents consume.

implementations.description: Reference implementations that exist under /patterns/<id>/. CI verifies each listed implementation directory exists and contains a COMPLIANCE.md.

guidance.description: Short do/don't items for generation-time guidance. Sub-normative: anything that belongs in CI or COMPLIANCE.md goes in `constraints` instead.

relatedPatterns.description: Ids of related patterns in this catalog. Referential existence is checked in CI.

references.description: External sources: ARIA APG, WCAG techniques, vendor guidelines, research.

exportMap.description: Framework → code symbol that owns this anatomy part (e.g. {"react": "CitationAnchor", "vanilla": "SourceAttribution.createAnchor"}). Mandatory on every part of a `kit` pattern; CI checks each named symbol exists in that framework's implementation.

description.description: What this part is and what it is responsible for.

required.description: Whether an implementation must render this part to claim compliance.

initial.description: Exactly one state per contract sets this to true.

transitionsTo.description: Ids of states reachable from this one. Omit for terminal states. Targets must exist in `states` (checked in CI).

id.description: Stable within the pattern. COMPLIANCE.md files reference this id; never reuse after removal.

level.description: RFC-2119 requirement level, normalized to five values.

statement.description: One atomic normative sentence containing the RFC-2119 keyword matching `level`. One rule per constraint — compound statements break compliance traceability.

rationale.description: Why this rule exists. Agents weigh constraints better when the reason ships with the rule.

category.description: The aspect of the implementation this rule governs.

verification.description: How an implementation proves compliance — the test, audit, or review step a COMPLIANCE.md should point at.

appliesTo.description: Restricts the rule to specific implementations. Omit when the rule applies to all.

wcagCriteria.description: WCAG success criteria this pattern implicates, each with why it applies here.

screenReader.description: What assistive technology users experience at each notable moment.

focusManagement.description: The pattern's focus strategy: where focus goes, and crucially where it must never go on its own.

relevance.description: Why this criterion applies to this pattern specifically.

when.description: The moment or event, e.g. "Stream completes".

behavior.description: What is announced or how the experience changes.
